title: Migrate impact plugin to contract v2
goal: Migrate plugins/agent/impact to contract v2: v2 result file on every exit path, disposition from router_reason_disposition, rc ∈ {0,1}, router budgets in manifest, name-matched inputs from engine index, signal handling for interruption path, and no artifact paths constructed in plugin code.

steps.description: Write the failing test for the v2 result contract: a unit test that stubs _impact_run_inner and asserts that impact_run writes a result_contract:2 JSON with verdict, disposition, and reason on every exit path (missing state_file → broken/broken, missing design.md → error/broken, router failure → timed_out/out_of_turns disposition, empty LLM response → error/broken, envelope malformed → incomplete/unusable, success → complete/complete). Run it and confirm it fails for the right reason before writing any implementation.

Write the failing test for disposition mapping: verify that every router reason string (router_timeout, router_out_of_turns, router_rate_limited, router_oom_kill, router_config_error, no_progress, unknown) maps to the correct ADR-054 §6a disposition word via router_reason_disposition, and that impact_run propagates those words into the result file. Run it and confirm it fails (impact_run does not call router_reason_disposition yet).

Write the failing grep test: assert that plugins/agent/impact/plugin.sh contains no hardcoded artifact paths constructed inside the run hook (no string literals of the form artifacts_dir/design.md, state_dir/scope-manifest.md, etc. built by the plugin). Run it and confirm it fails against the current plugin.sh.

Update plugins/agent/impact/manifest.yaml: (a) add result_contract: 2 under provides, (b) add a router: section under config with timeout_s: 600 and max_turns: 45 as manifest defaults (template override in simple.yaml already sets the same values and continues to win), (c) add a comment under hooks recording that cleanup is absent because impact holds no live resources.

Add _impact_write_result and _impact_input helpers to plugin.sh: _impact_write_result writes result_contract:2 JSON with verdict/disposition/reason/data to a path via atomic_write and sets _IMPACT_RESULT_WRITTEN; _impact_input reads a resolved input path from the ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS index (same pattern as plan's _plan_input). These are pure additions; nothing else changes in this step.

Rewrite impact_run to: (a) call stage_signal_begin/_impact_on_signal at entry and stage_signal_end at every return; (b) use ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR for the output directory instead of deriving it from state_file; (c) use _impact_input to read scope_manifest, design, and plan input paths from the engine's index instead of constructing them from state_dir/artifacts; (d) write a v2 result via _impact_write_result on every early-exit path (missing ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR → broken/broken, missing required input → broken/broken). Implement _impact_on_signal: writes interrupted/interrupted result if none written yet, then exits 1.

Update _impact_run_inner to write v2 results on all remaining exit paths: (a) router failure: call router_reason_disposition on _rc_reason and use that word as disposition; write result_contract:2 with verdict=error or incomplete as today but now also with disposition and reason fields; (b) empty LLM response: write result_contract:2, verdict=error, disposition=broken, reason=empty_response; (c) envelope schema failure / recovery: write result_contract:2 with disposition=unusable on malformed path, disposition=complete on recovered path; (d) prefilter merge failures: write result_contract:2, verdict=error, disposition=broken; (e) success path: write result_contract:2, verdict from jq, disposition=complete, reason from existing summary. Change all return 2 to return 1. Keep _IMPACT_RESULT_WRITTEN guard so signal handler does not double-write.

Run the three tests from steps 1–3 and confirm they now pass. Also run the full impact unit test suite (all tests/unit/impact-*.sh) and confirm no regressions. Run npm run test:unit. Fix any failures before proceeding.

Golden snapshot pass: run the existing impact integration or golden tests (tests/golden/ and tests/integration/ for impact, if any). If a snapshot diff is produced, capture the before state, apply the migration, re-run, and record the delta. If the output is structurally identical (same verdict/missing fields, extra result_contract+disposition+reason fields added), update the golden file. Acceptance: before/after diff shows only the new v2 fields appended; no verdict, missing[], or event sequence changes.

Run npm test (full bash test suite) and confirm green. Record the red step for each of the three new tests in the PR body (the assertion text and how it failed before the fix). Verify: grep over plugins/agent/impact/plugin.sh confirms no artifact paths constructed in code; manifest contains result_contract:2 and router: section; valid_verdicts covers complete, incomplete, error.

notes:
1. Router budget defaults in manifest (step-4): the issue says 'router budgets resolve from the manifest, and the template override still wins'. The manifest config.router values are the plugin's own defaults; the template's per-stage router: block already has the same values (timeout_s:600, max_turns:45, retries:1 in simple.yaml). The manifest values are a safety net when no template override exists — they do not conflict with the template because the template wins. retries:1 is NOT added to the manifest because the issue explicitly says impact 'no longer carries its own router.retries' (Folds in §, updated 2026-09-29). Only plan's manifest carries retry_on_exhaustion/retries.
2. Inputs (step-6): impact.run currently constructs '$state_dir/scope-manifest.md', '$artifacts_dir/design.md', '$artifacts_dir/plan.json'. With name-matched inputs the engine resolves those from the declared ids (scope_manifest, design, plan) and hands them in via ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS. The outer impact_run reads from the index; _impact_run_inner still takes explicit path args (unit-testable interface preserved).
3. Cleanup hook: impact holds no live resources (no spawned processes, no locks, no open handles beyond what atomic_write closes). The issue says 'if it has nothing to free, the hook is absent and that is recorded, not implied.' So no cleanup hook is added to manifest — instead a comment is added under hooks explaining this.
4. Golden snapshot (step-9): no golden files for impact were found in tests/golden/. If none exist, this step records that the before/after diff was verified by running the passing-run scenario manually and observing only additive field changes. The test confirming 'behaviour is unchanged' may be an existing integration test or a new one.
5. stage_signal_begin is already available via plugin-bootstrap.sh; no additional source line is needed in plugin.sh.
6. rc ∈ {0,1}: the current plugin uses return 2 in _impact_run_inner for contract-violation early exits. These all become return 1. impact_run currently returns 2 when state_file is absent — this becomes return 1 as well, after writing the v2 result.
7. 'data' field in v2 result: for impact, the relevant plugin-specific detail is the missing[] array and the verdict breakdown. The data field should carry at least missing_count on the non-error success path. For error/broken paths it can be an empty object {} or omit data entirely — teardown uses a targets array; plan omits data on failure paths.
8. The acceptance criterion 'Reddens at the merge-base' means the tests added in steps 1-3 must fail on the unmodified tree. The plan orders tests before implementation to satisfy this. The 'npm test green with the tree committed first' criterion means the full suite must pass after all changes are committed.
